geo.label: March lift-off priced; earnings dispersion
parts: Macro Stance

The US backdrop pits a Fed that has all but pre-announced a March lift-off against an earnings season splitting mega-cap growth into winners and casualties. CNBC read the Fed's January 26 statement as pointing to a rate hike coming in March, and Reuters reported that the Fed's Bullard sees three successive hikes to start the tightening cycle. [[n2074]] [[n2095]] Activity is not the constraint: CNBC reported weekly jobless claims of 238,000, fewer than expected, and the ISM manufacturing PMI stood at 57.6 index points in January. [[n2063]] [[n2028]] The constraint is the price of money. The S&P 500 fell 2.44% to 4,477.44 index points and the Nasdaq 100 lost 4.22% to 14,501.11 index points, while the VIX jumped 10.23% to 24.35 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03). Stance: Mixed, with supportive growth and hostile duration.
Rates & Curve

The 2Y yield closed at 1.19% and the 10Y at 1.82%, leaving the 10Y-2Y spread at +63 bps; over twenty observations the 2Y has risen 36 bps from 0.83% while the 10Y has added only 11 bps, so the spread has compressed by 25 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-03). The curve is still moderately steep, but the twenty-observation move is a bear flattening, with both legs up and the 2Y up more. The last five observations show just +1 bps on each, so the policy repricing has paused rather than reversed. Reuters' explainer on why the flattening matters and Standard Chartered's view that the curve could flatten and possibly invert this year frame the bear case, while Credit Suisse argues an inversion may be a 'false positive' recession signal. [[n2104]] [[n2090]] [[n2111]] The DXY slipped 0.58% to 95.38 index points and is down 1.93% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03), consistent with Reuters' read that the dollar rally had paused. [[n0033]]
New / Most Important

Meta Platforms (FB) delivered the defining shock. CNBC reported a 26% plunge, the stock's biggest one-day drop ever, and put the $232 billion fall as the largest one-day value drop in stock market history. [[n0811]] [[n1141]] Reuters said the wipe-out shook world tech stocks. [[n0842]] The after-hours tape was not uniformly grim: CNBC reported Amazon shares soaring on a cloud revenue beat and a huge profit gain from its Rivian stake. [[n0787]] Sarah Bloom Raskin's Fed nomination faces what The New York Times called a narrow path to confirmation. [[n2112]] The January jobs report is the next macro test, and Fox Business reported the White House warning that the Omicron spike could skew it. [[n2022]]
Playbook ✓

Action: stay underweight long-duration, ad-funded growth and overweight cash-generative energy and asset-sensitive financials. Trigger: keep the stance while the 2Y holds at or above its 1.19% close (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-03) and the VIX stays above the 19.73 index points it showed twenty sessions earlier (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03). What changes the call: a payrolls report weak enough to pull the 2Y back toward the 0.83% of twenty observations ago would argue for re-adding beaten-down growth. A strong print that lifts the 2Y faster than the 10Y would reinforce the tilt.

geo.label: ECB opens the door; BoE at 0.5%
parts: Macro Stance

[[n1259]] [[n1262]] In Frankfurt the ECB kept rates on hold, per DW.com, but Al Jazeera reported Christine Lagarde is no longer ruling out an interest-rate hike this year. [[n1263]] [[n0102]] For a region facing an energy shock, that is a meaningful shift in the reaction function.

The inflation impulse is energy-led and broadening. Bankier.pl noted European inflation surprised economists again, and Investing.com tied the euro's recovery to high eurozone inflation. [[n1663]] [[n1251]] Reuters' explainer on why Europe faces climbing energy bills, alongside its survey of efforts to shield households, shows the cost migrating onto budgets. [[n1267]] [[n1266]] Dutch TTF gas closed at 80.22 EUR/MWh, up 3.71% on the session but down 12.35% over twenty sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03), after The New York Times reported mostly US natural gas shipments easing Europe's energy crunch. [[n1499]] Intereconomics is already asking how large the risk of stagflation in the eurozone is. [[n1278]]
New / Most Important

Equities sold off as the hawkish turn met the Meta shock: the STOXX 600 fell 1.76% to 468.63 index points and the DAX 1.57% to 15,368.47 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03). Reuters reported ING's shares dipped 4% after earnings as provisions rose on inflation worries, while Shell hiked its dividend and boosted buybacks. [[n1145]] [[n0863]] Governor Bailey's warning that wage rises must slow, per Reuters, is the line that matters for front-end pricing. [[n1261]]
Playbook ✓

Action: prefer euro-area and UK banks and energy over rate-sensitive growth and autos, and keep duration short. Trigger: any further ECB signal that net purchases end sooner. What changes the call: a gas-supply shock that drives TTF back above the 91.52 EUR/MWh of twenty sessions ago (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03) would turn the hawkish pivot into a stagflation trap and favour defensives over banks.

geo.label: Easing bias into a holiday close
parts: Macro Stance

China enters the Year of the Tiger with policy leaning against a soft growth tape while the onshore market is shut for the Lunar New Year. The Shanghai Composite's last completed session left it at 3,361.44 index points, down 0.97% on the day and 7.12% over twenty sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-28). The Hang Seng finished its last pre-holiday session up 1.07% at 23,802.26 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31), and the South China Morning Post noted the index logged a January gain while closing the Year of the Ox with a slump. [[n0164]] The stance is Mixed: easing is real, but the Olympics open inside what PBS called a fortress against COVID, and zero-COVID still caps services demand. [[n0199]]
PMIs & Activity

January's surveys confirmed that momentum faded into the holiday. Reuters reported factory activity growth slowing as demand waned with COVID surging, while the Caixin PMI showed outright contraction as lockdowns bit. [[n0148]] [[n0144]] ABN AMRO concluded that the January PMIs indicate quarter-on-quarter growth will drop in the first quarter. [[n0157]] That follows 2021 GDP growth of 8.1%, the fastest in a decade per Global Times, and fixed-asset investment growth of 4.9% per Macau Business, so the base is high and the slowdown is in the second derivative. [[n0116]] [[n0118]] HSBC told CNBC that disruptions in China can create ripple effects across the global supply chain, which keeps the PMI story relevant for European autos and Asian semis. [[n0162]]
Credit Impulse

The credit impulse is being pushed from the top. CNBC reported the central bank cut key lending rates, including one for the first time in nearly two years, and Fibre2Fashion detailed cuts to medium-term loan and reverse repo rates. [[n0122]] [[n0125]] Bloomberg framed the move as China's central bank seizing the moment for stimulus while the Fed hikes. [[n0127]] MacroMicro's tracking of loan prime rate swaps is the market gauge of whether further cuts are being priced. [[n0198]] The mechanism matters: cheaper funding becomes a credit impulse only if developers and local governments can and will borrow, and with property sales weak the transmission is slower than headline rate cuts imply. The next aggregate financing release, rather than another rate trim, is the real test.
Property

Property remains the drag that easing must overcome. Caixin described China's property market as off to a bleak start in 2022, and Business Recorder reported new home prices fell less in December on promotions and easing curbs. [[n0191]] [[n0113]] The Evergrande workout is now a creditor story: The Real Deal reported Oaktree Capital seized a second Evergrande property, and Reuters chronicled the dashed dreams of the developer's showpiece resort island. [[n0182]] [[n0166]] MoneyWeek went as far as recommending a short in China's largest real estate broker. [[n0192]] Policy is stabilising financing at the margin but not yet sales, so developer credit remains a distressed-asset trade rather than a beta trade.
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

Policy runs on two tracks. The Wall Street Journal reported Xi Jinping seeks to scale China's 'three big mountains' to achieve common prosperity, an agenda the Lowy Institute calls a Catch-22. [[n0215]] [[n0161]] Trade friction persists, with Reuters quoting a US trade official who says China failed to meet its Phase 1 commitments. [[n0186]] Externally China keeps exporting capital and capacity: Reuters reported an $8 billion nuclear power plant deal in Argentina, and Reuters columnist Andy Home noted China's metals imports boomed in 2021 and so did its exports. [[n1869]] [[n0204]] The tech crackdown remains a governance overhang; the South China Morning Post reported the JD.com founder's US$2 billion charity donation against that backdrop. [[n0209]]
Markets & Flows

With onshore trading closed, US-listed proxies are doing the price discovery. KWEB closed at 35.84 USD, down 2.00% on the session but up 6.60% over twenty sessions, and FXI is up 6.78% at 37.63 USD, while the A-share tracker ASHR is down 4.69% over the same span at 36.34 USD. Alibaba's ADR is up 10.45% over five sessions at 123.47 USD and JD.com's ADR is up 14.01% over twenty sessions at 71.85 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03). In Hong Kong's last pre-holiday session Tencent rose 2.43% to 447.54 HKD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-31). Electric vehicles are a bright spot: the South China Morning Post reported sales surging at Xpeng, Li Auto and NIO, and CNBC said Xpeng delivered over 10,000 cars for a fifth straight month. [[n0609]] [[n0534]]
New / Most Important

The Winter Olympics open inside a closed loop, with Axios warning that COVID threatens China's Olympic prestige and the official Olympics site publishing opening-ceremony start times. [[n0175]] [[n0200]] For markets, the most important item is the policy divergence: Beijing is easing as Washington tightens, and the gap between offshore internet strength and onshore weakness will be tested when the mainland reopens. George Soros' warning, reported by CNN, that China is facing an economic crisis is the bear case in its starkest form. [[n0163]]
Playbook ✓

Action: hold a modest, volatility-sized overweight in offshore internet and EV names through KWEB-style exposure, and stay underweight developers and onshore cyclicals. Trigger: add only if onshore indices stabilise on reopening and credit data show transmission beyond rate cuts. What changes the call: a COVID disruption around the Games or a cascade of developer defaults would argue for cutting the offshore overweight. ⚠ Divergence: KWEB is up 6.60% and FXI 6.78% over twenty sessions, yet ASHR is down 4.69% and the Shanghai Composite 7.12% over comparable spans (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03; Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-01-28), and the Caixin PMI is contracting even as the central bank eases. Offshore optimism is running ahead of onshore evidence.

geo.label: BOJ anchored; energy-import squeeze
parts: Macro Stance

The currency channel runs through the energy bill. Reuters reported Japan's December exports and imports hit record highs by value as supply bottlenecks eased, and The Seattle Times attributed record imports to surging energy prices. [[n1436]] [[n1437]] That squeeze is landing on utilities, which Reuters said are reeling, some more than others, as sky-high fuel prices hit earnings. [[n1059]] With the DXY down 1.93% over five sessions at 95.38 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03), the dollar's pause offers only marginal relief; the terms-of-trade loss is about the price of fuel. Corporate signals are split: Barron's said Sony's profits soared on Spider-Man despite PlayStation problems, but PCMag reported the chip shortage forced Sony to slash its PS5 shipment forecast, and the shares fell 6.08% to 12,585.00 JPY (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03). [[n0742]] [[n1870]] Toyota rose 0.88% to 2,293.50 JPY (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03) after Reuters reported it remains the world's biggest car seller. [[n0313]]

The break is that companies with subscription or brand power are still passing costs through; CBS News counted Starbucks' latest increase as its third price hike since October. [[n1163]] The losers are businesses whose cost base outruns pricing, which keeps the stance Mixed.

The convention says staples are bond proxies that suffer when yields rise. With the front end driving rates and real incomes squeezed, staples are trading as inflation pass-through vehicles instead. Bullish relative to discretionary, with the risk that volumes crack under repeated price rises.

earnings_pattern.title: Engagement and guidance beat the beat
parts: Rewarded

The market paid for evidence of durable demand and pricing. Reuters reported Google propelled record Alphabet revenue and drove the shares up 8%, and CNBC said Alphabet announced a 20-for-1 stock split. [[n0086]] [[n0577]] AMD rose 10% after a strong 2022 sales outlook, and UPS shares hit a record high after an outstanding 2021, per Reuters. [[n0515]] [[n0629]] After Thursday's close, Reuters said Pinterest's results dazzled Wall Street, and TechCrunch greeted Snap's report with 'Snap finally did it'. [[n0856]] [[n1161]]
Punished

Disappointment on users or guidance was punished brutally. Meta Platforms (FB) fell 26.39% to 237.76 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03) after The Guardian reported Facebook's first-ever drop in daily users. [[n1090]] CNBC reported PayPal's plunge on weak earnings guidance, and Payments Dive said it scrapped its account growth goal. [[n0602]] [[n0732]] Spotify sank on first-quarter subscriber numbers, and Bloomberg said EA's revenue forecast missed estimates after the Battlefield flop. [[n0745]] [[n0552]]
Pattern

The common thread is that the market is valuing the next four quarters, not the last one. Companies that showed engagement growth or pricing power, as Amazon did with what CNBC described as a nearly 17% Prime price increase, were rewarded. [[n0784]] Companies that revealed user stagnation, platform dependence or guidance cuts were punished regardless of the reported quarter. The Apple privacy change, which Business Insider said Facebook blames for a $10 billion cost, is the clearest example of a structural rather than cyclical miss. [[n1138]]
Attention into EPS

Expectations were set high for the mega-caps. GeekWire's preview said analysts expected record Amazon revenue of $137B with lower profits, so the reaction hinges on cloud and advertising quality rather than the headline. [[n0523]] Smart money was split on fintech: Wolfe Research's Darrin Peller told CNBC he believes there will be consistency to PayPal's growth, a view now tested by the stock's record one-day fall. [[n0637]] The next prints that matter test the same engagement filter, including Uber, where ig.com previewed what to expect from fourth-quarter results. [[n0089]]
Playbook

Action: buy post-earnings drawdowns only where guidance held and engagement grew, and avoid catching user-metric breakdowns. Trigger: a gap down on a beat with intact guidance is the entry signal; a gap down on lowered guidance is not. What changes the call: a broad recovery in the Nasdaq 100 toward the 15,771.78 index points of twenty sessions ago (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03) would signal that rates, not fundamentals, were driving the dispersion.

underowned.title: Euro-area and UK banks after the ECB pivot
parts: Attention Gap

While attention fixed on the Meta collapse, Lagarde's refusal to rule out a 2022 hike and the Bank of England's second consecutive increase shifted the earnings base for European lenders. [[n0102]] [[n0790]] Societe Generale rose 1.74% to 34.26 EUR and is up 4.28% over twenty sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03).
Exposure & Risk

Exposure runs through rate-sensitive retail and corporate lenders such as Societe Generale and HSBC, at 546.30 GBp. The risk is credit: the Jersey Evening Post reported the Bank's hike came as households face the worst income hit since at least 1990, and banks with central and eastern European franchises sit closest to the Ukraine standoff. [[n1310]]
Trigger to Watch

Watch Lagarde's follow-up remarks, which Reuters covered from the press conference, and whether the market starts pricing an end to net asset purchases. [[n1270]] A failure of bank shares to rise on further hawkish guidance would mean credit fears have taken over.

underowned.title: Fertilizer and farm inputs as a supply-shock hedge

Watch potash and grain export headlines tied to Belarus and the Black Sea; Successful Farming reported an analyst warning grain exports are likely disrupted in a Russia-Ukraine conflict. [[n1801]] A move by CBOT wheat back above its 760.75 US cents/bu level of twenty sessions ago (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03) would confirm the premium is rebuilding.

crypto.title: Bitcoin steadies while crypto plumbing cracks
parts: Market Context

Bitcoin is stabilising rather than recovering. It closed at 37,154.60 USD, up 0.55% on the day but down 13.79% over twenty sessions from 43,099.70 USD, while Ether closed at 2,679.16 USD, down 19.06%, and Solana at 101.46 USD, down 30.58% (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-03). Listed proxies have fallen harder: Coinbase is down 22.59% over twenty sessions at 181.31 USD, MicroStrategy 33.20% at 340.09 USD and GBTC 24.19% at 22.25 USD, and miners are weaker still, with Marathon Digital down 28.39% and Riot Blockchain 31.02% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03). The asset class is trading as a leveraged extension of the Nasdaq, not as a hedge against it.
New / Most Important

The infrastructure news is negative. CNBC reported more than $320 million stolen in the latest apparent crypto hack, and The Defiant said Jump Crypto replaced over $320M of Wormhole wrapped ETH in a DeFi bailout. [[n0950]] [[n0962]] Bloomberg reported the biggest Texas bitcoin miner shut down ahead of a cold blast. [[n0944]] Regulation is advancing on several fronts: Reuters said India will tax cryptocurrencies at 30%, and Bloomberg reported Russia values local crypto at $200 billion as rules near. [[n0932]] [[n0936]] Private capital is still flowing, as CNBC reported FTX hitting a $32 billion valuation despite bear market fears, and Reuters said Stocktwits rolled out crypto trading. [[n0438]] [[n1762]] The Boston Fed's Project Hamilton phase-one summary on a central-bank digital currency keeps an official alternative to private stablecoins on the agenda. [[n2121]]
Playbook

Action: stay underweight crypto beta and prefer spot exposure over miners and leveraged wrappers; the futures-based BITO, down 17.37% over twenty sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03), is a cleaner proxy than the miners. Trigger: re-engage only if Bitcoin reclaims its 43,099.70 USD level of twenty sessions ago (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-03) while the Nasdaq 100 stabilises. What changes the call: regulatory clarity of the kind Michael Saylor told CNBC would speed institutional adoption would support a re-rating, whereas another bridge exploit on the Wormhole scale would extend the drawdown. [[n0665]]

flows.title: Liquidity is being withdrawn from the front end
parts: Global Liquidity

Global liquidity is turning from abundant to rationed, and the withdrawal is now explicit. Reuters detailed how the Bank of England plans to reverse QE by giving up gilts, and ING Think published its guide to the Bank's quantitative tightening. [[n1238]] [[n1226]] The Economist argued quantitative tightening is no substitute for higher interest rates, and the Bank of England is now pursuing both. [[n1286]] Reuters commentary that the second BoE rate rise sounds a 'QT' klaxon captures the shift from price to quantity. [[n1192]] The St. Louis Fed's analysis of whether Fed asset purchases reshaped bank balance sheets frames the risk: reserves created by QE sit on bank balance sheets, and their drain tightens conditions beyond the policy rate. [[n1297]] For equities, the drain matters most for long-duration names whose valuations were built on cheap balance-sheet capacity. China is the counter-current, with Bloomberg describing its central bank seizing the moment for stimulus. [[n0127]]
Rates & Dollar

The rates signal is a front-end shock. The 2Y has risen 36 bps over twenty observations to 1.19%, the 10Y 11 bps to 1.82%, and the 10Y-2Y spread has compressed 25 bps to +63 bps in a bear flattening (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-03). Duration ETFs reflect it: TLT fell 0.78% to 141.09 USD and IEF 0.43% to 112.06 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03). The dollar is not amplifying the squeeze, with the DXY down 1.93% over five sessions at 95.38 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03), which Reuters described as the rally taking a pause. [[n0033]] Emerging markets remain exposed: Al Jazeera reported looming Fed hikes have emerging markets dreading deja vu, and EMB is down 1.91% over twenty sessions at 104.85 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03). [[n2073]] Phenomenal World's essay on acute dollar dominance is a reminder that dollar funding remains the global constraint, so a DXY rebound would tighten conditions faster than any single central bank. [[n1308]]
Credit Check

Credit is where the flow evidence is strongest. Reuters reported US high-yield bond ETFs saw record outflows in January, and HYG is down 2.30% over twenty sessions at 84.10 USD while LQD is down 2.87% at 126.71 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03). [[n1301]] Reuters noted tech-light corporate bonds swerved the worst of the stock market woes, so the damage is a rates repricing rather than a default scare. [[n1246]] Bloomberg's warning that mortgage bond weakness threatens the US corporate debt market identifies the contagion channel: as agency MBS cheapen, relative-value buyers can demand wider corporate spreads. [[n2079]] LSEG's primer on corporate bond default risk is timely, but defaults are not yet the issue; spreads are widening in sympathy with rates, which keeps investment grade preferable to high yield. [[n1289]]
Equity & Fund Flows

Equity flows show rotation and capital return rather than wholesale exit. Bloomberg flagged that the Meta drop could hit stock funds with $1 trillion that bet on the Facebook parent, a concentration risk for index-heavy portfolios. [[n0837]] Corporate buybacks are the steady bid, with Euronews reporting Nokia resuming its dividend and share buybacks and ExxonMobil initiating a $10 billion repurchase. [[n0851]] [[n1296]] New issuance is retreating: Global Finance Magazine reported IPOs delivered their worst returns in a decade, and Bloomberg said struggling IPOs gave FTX's chief pause on going public. [[n1285]] [[n0938]] Active managers are split, as Bloomberg reported AQR's absolute return fund had a record month with a 15.4% return while ARK kept adding Tesla ($6M) and Xpeng ($0.5M) shares, per eletric-vehicles.com. [[n1865]] [[n0671]] Bloomberg reported Rob Citrone's Discovery Capital gained 4% in January on the market's value move, while Business Insider said the hedge fund that lost nearly $7 billion betting against stocks like GameStop is raising cash for a new long-only fund. [[n1881]] [[n0621]]
Portfolio Implication

The implication is to own cash flow now and duration later. Keep fixed-income duration short while the 2Y leads, prefer investment-grade over high yield given record outflows, and in equities favour buyback-funded energy, staples and asset-sensitive banks over long-duration growth. Reassess when the 2Y stops rising faster than the 10Y or when high-yield outflows reverse; either would signal that the front-end shock has been absorbed. Within equities, prefer companies funding buybacks from free cash flow over those reliant on new issuance, since weak IPO returns show marginal equity supply is being priced at a discount.

anticipatory.title: January payrolls under an Omicron cloud
parts: What Is Priced

The front end has already priced a March start, with the 2Y up 36 bps over twenty observations to 1.19% (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-03). CME Group's review of rate-hike expectations versus reality frames the debate, and CNBC's report of 238,000 jobless claims, fewer than expected, argues the labour market is tight. [[n2105]] [[n2063]]
Conditional Expression

If the January jobs report is distorted lower by Omicron, as the White House warned, while wages stay firm, the March path should survive and the bear flattening extend; express that through financials over the Nasdaq 100. [[n2022]] If the report is strong, the 2Y could push higher and favour XLF over XLRE. Only a weak print with soft wages would justify adding duration.
Risk

The risk is misreading noise as signal. An Omicron-distorted headline could trigger a knee-jerk rally in duration that reverses once wage data are digested. With the VIX at 24.35 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03), positions should be sized for a two-way move.

anticipatory.title: Russia's Belarus drills and Europe's energy premium

Conditional Expression

If the drills NATO says will involve 30,000 Russian troops in Belarus escalate into an incursion, expect European gas, oil, defence and gold to rise while Polish assets and euro-area cyclicals fall. [[n1418]] PBS reported US intelligence suggests Russia is plotting a false-flag attack as a pretext, which makes the scenario plausible enough for a hedge in TTF or defence rather than an outright bet. [[n1502]] If diplomacy holds, fade the oil premium first.

The risk is paying for protection that decays. The Economist's question of how Europe would cope if Russia cuts off its gas is already familiar, and The New York Times reported mostly US shipments easing the crunch. [[n1205]] [[n1499]]

anticipatory.title: The first full session after Amazon, Pinterest, Snap and Ford

The regular session priced contagion from Meta: Amazon fell 7.81% to 2,776.91 USD, Snap 23.60% to 24.50 USD, Pinterest 10.32% to 24.51 USD and Ford 3.59% to 19.89 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03). If Amazon's after-hours strength holds into the cash session, it validates the data-ownership divide and supports the long Amazon versus XLY pair set out below. GeekWire's note that Amazon would have posted a $1.8 billion operating loss without AWS argues for owning it as a cloud and advertising story, not a retail one. [[n0788]] If Ford's skid persists despite what The New York Times said was $17.9 billion of 2021 earnings bolstered by Rivian, the market is discounting non-operating gains. [[n0813]]

After-hours moves on thin liquidity can reverse at the open, and Meta's follow-through could overwhelm single-stock news.

anticipatory.title: China's return from the Lunar New Year

The risk is a COVID outbreak inside or around the Olympic bubble, which the BBC described in detail, or a fresh tech-regulatory headline. [[n0201]] Either would hit the offshore names that have rallied most.

catalysts.title: Meta Platforms (FB): from growth compounder to show-me story
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Meta's problem is structural. Shacknews reported its Reality Labs division lost $3.3 billion in the fourth quarter, and Business Insider said Zuckerberg sees unprecedented competition from TikTok. [[n1089]] [[n1166]] Add the Apple privacy hit and the first user decline, and the market is repricing Meta as a mature ad business funding an expensive bet.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The shares closed at 237.76 USD after a 26.39% fall, against 324.17 USD twenty sessions earlier (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03). Business Insider noted Meta plunged below Berkshire Hathaway in market value for the first time in nearly two years. [[n0841]] The risk to a short is value buying and buybacks after such a reset.
Trade Expression
Avoid bottom-fishing; express the view as a pair, long Alphabet against short Meta, so the trade isolates data ownership rather than market direction. Revisit if user numbers stabilise.

catalysts.title: Amazon (AMZN): cloud and pricing reset the bar
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Amazon's report showed where the profit pool sits. Shacknews said AWS revenue rose 40% to $17.78 billion, CNBC reported a $31 billion a year advertising business, and the Prime price rise lifts recurring revenue. [[n0099]] [[n1128]]

The stock closed at 2,776.91 USD after a 7.81% fall, well below the 3,287.14 USD of twenty sessions ago (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03). GeekWire's point that profits nearly doubled thanks to the Rivian stake is the risk: the headline profit includes non-operating gains that cannot be relied on to recur. [[n0785]]
Trade Expression

Buy on confirmation that after-hours gains hold through the first full session, sizing modestly given volatility, and pair against the XLY ETF to isolate the cloud and advertising engine from the consumer cycle.

catalysts.title: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD): execution through the semis storm

AMD is executing while the sector sells off. Tom's Hardware headlined 2022 sales of $21.5 billion alongside the best quarter in AMD's history, and CEO Lisa Su told CNBC the company grew in every business. [[n1040]] [[n1076]] Notebookcheck said AMD expects record 2022 earnings as it closes in on Intel's profit margins. [[n1077]]

The shares closed at 120.08 USD, down 2.18% on the session but up 17.04% over five sessions, against 136.15 USD twenty sessions earlier (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03). The risk is sector beta: the PHLX Semiconductor Index fell 4.58% on the same session.

Accumulate on sector-driven pullbacks rather than chasing, with a hedge in SOXX to neutralise the high-bar dynamic that hit peers after Qualcomm. A break below the prior close would delay entry.

catalysts.title: PayPal (PYPL): a guidance reset breaks the growth narrative
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

PayPal's guidance cut changed the narrative. Forbes reported the crash wiped out over $50 billion in market value after the company lowered its profit outlook, and separately that PayPal admitted 4.5 million accounts were illegitimate. [[n0730]] [[n1108]] The account-growth story that justified the multiple is gone.

Prefer the networks: long Visa or Mastercard against short PayPal captures the gap between transaction volume growth and wallet engagement.

catalysts.title: Shell (SHEL.L): buybacks as the energy dividend
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Shell is converting high prices into shareholder cash. The New York Times reported its profit jumped on higher oil and natural gas prices, and Reuters said it began trading under a simpler single-line share structure. [[n1159]] [[n0478]] The simplified structure should broaden the buyer base for the buyback.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The shares rose 1.43% to 1,960.00 GBp and are up 14.07% over twenty sessions from 1,718.20 GBp (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03). The risk is political: Reuters described Europe's efforts to shield households from soaring energy costs, which could put producer profits in the line of fire. [[n1266]]
Trade Expression

Hold an overweight while Brent stays above the 80.80 USD/bbl of twenty sessions ago (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03); reduce if gas prices collapse or if policymakers target producer profits directly.

catalysts.title: Sony Group (6758.T): content strength, hardware bottleneck
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Sony's earnings show the split between content and hardware. Barron's reported profits soared on the strength of the Spider-Man franchise despite PlayStation problems, and CNBC said Sony agreed to buy Bungie in a $3.6 billion deal as industry consolidation heats up. [[n0742]] [[n0483]]
Price Hurdle & Risk

The shares fell 6.08% to 12,585.00 JPY and are down 18.91% over twenty sessions from 15,520.00 JPY (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03). The risk is the chip shortage capping console volumes, which PCMag said forced a cut to the PS5 shipment forecast. [[n1870]]
Trade Expression
Accumulate gradually for the content and gaming franchise, but only after the shares stabilise; a further break would signal that hardware constraints dominate the content story.
